business.title: Gold heads for steep weekly loss as Hormuz tensions lift crude toward five-month highs - Kitco AM Report
business.description: (Kitco NewsWire) – Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in early U.S. trading Friday, extending Thursday's heavy losses as renewed Middle East tensions pushed crude oil prices higher and reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain restrictive monetary policy. Gold failed to attract sustained safe-haven demand despite growing geopolitical risks and weakness in global equities, while silver faced additional pressure from concerns about industrial activity and elevated borrowing costs. At the latest available morning price reading, spot gold was trading near $4,026.56 an ounce, down 2.40% on the quoted session, while spot silver was trading near $53.801, down 6.40%. Gold was heading toward a weekly loss of more than 3.5%, with both metals remaining under heavy selling pressure.Market positioning remains dominated by persistent inflation pressure and expectations for further monetary tightening. September consumer prices rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% annually, while producer prices increased 1.3% and 6.3%, respectively. Interest rate futures indicate that the Fed is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at its Oct. 27-28 meeting, although traders continue to assign approximately a 78% probability to at least one additional increase by December. Thursday's sharp technology-led equity selloff encouraged demand for government bonds, producing a substantial decline in Treasury yields. However, the benchmark 10-year yield rebounded toward the 5.0% area Friday as renewed energy-price increases revived inflation concerns. The combination of firm rate expectations, rising crude prices and continued liquidation pressure has limited gold's ability to benefit from geopolitical uncertainty or intermittent declines in yields.The Federal Reserve remains in its premeeting communications blackout, shifting attention toward Friday's preliminary October manufacturing and services purchasing managers' indexes at 9:45 a.m. EDT and the final University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey at 10 a.m. EDT. The business activity reports will provide fresh evidence on economic growth, employment conditions and input-price pressures, while the consumer survey will offer another assessment of inflation expectations.The Strait of Hormuz and U.S.-Iran situation remains a significant source of volatility in global energy markets, with renewed attacks on commercial shipping and threats against regional oil infrastructure raising concerns about additional supply disruptions. Maritime traffic through the strategic waterway has slowed following attacks involving tankers operated by major Gulf energy companies, while negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain stalled over sanctions, maritime access and broader security arrangements. Reports concerning possible further U.S. and Israeli military action against Iranian targets have added to market uncertainty, although no new operation has been confirmed. The latest escalation has reinforced concerns about the reliability of oil exports through the Persian Gulf, despite producers' continued efforts to reroute shipments through alternative infrastructure. Brent crude briefly climbed toward $115.00 a barrel, its highest level in approximately five months, while WTI moved above $100.00.For gold, the renewed escalation creates competing influences. The threat of additional military confrontation and disruptions to energy supplies supports defensive demand, but higher crude prices also increase the risk of persistent inflation and additional Fed tightening. This has limited the metal's traditional response to geopolitical uncertainty, with investors directing some defensive flows toward U.S. government bonds. Silver has suffered considerably greater selling pressure as the precious metals decline coincides with concerns that higher energy costs and restrictive monetary policy could weaken manufacturing activity. The sharp divergence between geopolitical risk and bullion performance underscores the current importance of interest rate expectations, liquidity and portfolio positioning.Global equity markets were weaker before the U.S. open, extending Thursday's technology-led selloff as investors reassessed artificial intelligence investment spending, corporate financing requirements and elevated valuations. S&P 500 futures declined approximately 0.3%, while Dow futures were down around 0.7% and Nasdaq futures slipped approximately 0.1%. The declines followed Thursday's 2.60% drop in the Nasdaq Composite and 1.21% loss in the S&P 500. European equities were also under pressure amid higher energy prices and weaker regional business activity readings, while Asian markets remained volatile as technology shares continued to struggle. Concerns about France's fiscal position and elevated European borrowing costs added to the cautious tone. Strong demand for government bonds during the previous session contrasted with continued weakness in precious metals, reflecting divergent reactions to inflation and financial-market risks.The key outside markets see Nymex WTI crude oil prices higher and trading near $101.10 a barrel, while Brent crude was near $114.72. The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is trading near the 5.0% area following Thursday's sharp decline and Friday's partial rebound. The U.S. dollar index is firmer, trading near 101.76, with safe-haven demand and expectations for restrictive Fed policy continuing to support the greenback. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.)Technically, spot gold bulls' next upside price objective is to push prices back above the $4,075.00 to $4,080.00 resistance zone, with a sustained move targeting $4,200.00 and then $4,250.00. Bears' next near-term downside price objective is a break below the $3,963.00 to $3,946.00 support zone, with deeper downside targets at $3,890.00 and then $3,500.00. First resistance is seen at $4,075.00 and then at $4,080.00. First support is seen at $3,963.00 and then at $3,946.00.Spot silver bulls' next upside price objective is to drive prices back above the $54.530 to $55.770 resistance zone, with a move above that area targeting $58.090 and then $60.000. The next downside price objective for the bears is a break below $53.460, with deeper downside targets at $52.410 and then $51.390. First resistance is seen at $54.530 and then at $55.770. Next support is seen at $53.460 and then at $52.410.See live precious metals prices for gold, silver, platinum and palladium — in USD, CAD and 12 more currencies.

science.title: Efficient real-time vehicle tracking via lightweight YOLO and DeepSORT integration
science.description: Detecting and tracking vehicles ahead during driving is a critical technology for ensuring driving safety and enhancing the driving experience. However, traditional detection and tracking models often suffer from high computational intensity and large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained mobile devices. This paper introduces a lightweight vehicle tracking model that integrates YOLO and DeepSORT. By incorporating GhostConv and C3GhostV2 modules into the backbone and neck networks of YOLO, we enhance detection accuracy while reducing model size. The Focal-EIoU function is utilized to improve the recognition of small, distant target vehicles. Additionally, ShuffleNetV2 replaces DeepSORT’s feature extraction network, further reducing model parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that among the latest models in the YOLO series, YOLOv5 offers more stable and accurate performance, making it a more suitable baseline for vehicle detection and tracking tasks. Based on this foundation, experimental results show that, compared to the baseline model implemented using the Ultralytics framework, the proposed model reduces GFLOPs by 37.1%, decreases the number of parameters by 34.5%, and achieves mAP@0.5 by 0.3%. The overall model size is only 13.62 MB, 44.8% smaller than the original. Validated on the SODA10M dataset, the model exhibits improved detection accuracy and maintains performance compared to other models, making it suitable for deployment on mobile devices during vehicle driving.

science.title: Technology-based structural racism and telehealth video usage among primary care patients
science.description: We tested whether technology-based structural racism mechanisms (digital redlining, path dependency, technical difficulties) were associated with lower telehealth video visit rates (versus audio-only; in-person visits excluded) among Black compared to White patients. Using structured and unstructured electronic health record data from 137,297 patients with completed telehealth visits over 26.5 months linked with broadband market data, we examined correlates of racial differences in video versus audio-only visits. Patient race had no significant unadjusted effect, but adjustment for individual and zip code level confounders revealed a 6% reduction in video visit rate ratios for Black patients, widening to 7–9% with interaction terms. For digital redlining, broadband market conditions were worse in areas with high neighborhood disadvantage and Black residential composition. However, broadband conditions were not associated with video visit rates. For path dependency, portal nonenrollment was more common among Black patients but had a stronger negative association with video visit rates among White patients. For technical difficulties, Black patients experienced more difficulties, which were associated with greater odds of a subsequent audio-only visit—particularly among Black patients. Findings suggest technology-based structural racism may operate through conditional and sequential mechanisms across telehealth stages. Health systems should monitor multilevel telehealth inequities across care stages.
